req.title: Index renders even with zero posts
req.statement: The system shall render the index page with 'No posts' or empty state when the post table is empty.
triggers: index renders even with zero posts

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-037 requires the index page (GET /) to render successfully (HTTP 2xx) even when the post table is empty. Three tests are designed: (1) a positive test confirming HTTP 200 with an empty post table — the core requirement; (2) a negative test confirming that a client-side bad method (POST /) returns HTTP 405, exercising the error pathway; (3) a boundary test confirming the transition from zero posts to one post, verifying the empty-state disappears and the post appears — this is a state-transition boundary at count=0 vs count=1. All tests use an in-process Flask test client with a fresh temp database initialised via init_db(), ensuring the post table is truly empty for the zero-post cases. Assertions are exact-value to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_index_empty_db_returns_200
preconditions: Application is created with TESTING=True and a fresh empty database (no posts, no users)
Database schema is initialised via init_db() so tables exist but are empty
actions: Send GET / with the Flask test client
trace: R-FLASKR-037: index renders even with zero posts -> HTTP 2xx response
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert len(r.data) > 0
assert b'text/html' in r.content_type.encode() or 'text/html' in r.content_type
os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_index_boundary_zero_to_one_post
preconditions: Application is created with TESTING=True and a fresh empty database
Database schema is initialised via init_db()
A user is inserted so a post can be authored
actions: Verify GET / returns 200 with empty post table (count=0)
Insert exactly one post directly into the database
Verify GET / returns 200 and the post title appears in the response (count=1)
expected: At count=0: HTTP 200, post title b'BoundaryTitle' absent from response
At count=1: HTTP 200, post title b'BoundaryTitle' present in response
trace: R-FLASKR-037: boundary at zero posts -> one post; state transition from empty to non-empty
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db, get_db
from werkzeug.security import generate_password_hash

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r0 = client.get('/')
assert r0.status_code == 200
assert b'BoundaryTitle' not in r0.data

with app.app_context():
    db = get_db()
    db.execute("INSERT INTO user (username, password) VALUES (?, ?)",
               ('buser', generate_password_hash('bpass')))
    db.commit()
    uid = db.execute("SELECT id FROM user WHERE username='buser'").fetchone()[0]
    db.execute("INSERT INTO post (title, body, author_id) VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
               ('BoundaryTitle', 'BoundaryBody', uid))
    db.commit()

r1 = client.get('/')
assert r1.status_code == 200
assert b'BoundaryTitle' in r1.data
os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_index_empty_db_exact_status_not_redirect
preconditions: Application is created with TESTING=True and a fresh empty database
Database schema is initialised via init_db()
No user is logged in (anonymous client)
actions: Send GET / as an anonymous (unauthenticated) client with follow_redirects=False
expected: HTTP status code is exactly 200 (not a redirect 301/302)
No Location header pointing away from /
trace: R-FLASKR-037: anonymous client on empty DB -> direct 200, no redirect
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
r = client.get('/', follow_redirects=False)
assert r.status_code == 200
assert r.status_code != 301
assert r.status_code != 302
assert r.status_code != 404
assert r.status_code != 500
location = r.headers.get('Location', '')
assert '/auth/login' not in location
os.unlink(path)

tests.name: test_index_empty_db_decision_table_get_vs_delete
preconditions: Application is created with TESTING=True and a fresh empty database
Database schema is initialised via init_db()
actions: Send DELETE / (unsupported method) to verify 4xx is returned
Send GET / to confirm 200 is returned for the correct method
trace: R-FLASKR-037: decision table — only GET is allowed on /; other methods yield 4xx
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app
from flaskr.db import init_db

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix='.sqlite')
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()
rd = client.delete('/')
assert rd.status_code == 405
assert rd.status_code != 200

rg = client.get('/')
assert rg.status_code == 200
assert rg.status_code != 405
os.unlink(path)
